status: issued on 21 October 2026 (provisional codes, confirmed by residents)

criteria.text: Easy for citizens to remember their code, and even easier to get it: a place word they already use + a short number read in pairs; the code is shown, shared and plated without effort.
The addressable unit is the compound behind its gate, with structures, entrances and flats as sub-units.

Use the government's addresses wherever they exist (Campost PLP/FindMe, council numbering) and create nothing new there; N-Ways codes only where nothing official exists; a later official address becomes primary and the N-Ways code an alias.
A code never moves and is never reused; zones and area numbers are append-only and frozen against reforms.
Every name, form and spoken form in French and English; English first in the North-West and South-West.
Spot codes computed on the phone; home codes from small per-area registry files.
Method, engine and code data public under open licences (to decide).
Codes describe places, never people; extra safety rules in the North-West, South-West and conflict-affected border areas.

verdict.postcodes: In name only: commune postal codes announced by Campost/FindMe in Nov 2024, no published format or list; the UPU format (2002) has none; mail goes to P.O. boxes ('BP 6000 YAOUNDÉ').
verdict.addresses: Partial: Douala metric door numbering since 1992 (under 15% of roads named in 2019), Yaoundé numbered streets ('Rue 1794'); no national register or law.

campost.rule: Filled when Campost publishes its commune codes or a resident gives their PLP; N-Ways codes nest inside the commune code, never replace it.

interoperation.poBox: A BP is stored as a mailbox of a person or organisation, never as a place.

patterns: Douala and Yaoundé: dense one-storey houses in walled or unwalled parcelles, immeubles in Akwa, Bonanjo, Bonapriso, Bastos, centre-ville; wooden houses (maisons en planches) in older Douala quartiers
North, Far North, Adamaoua: saré — walled family compounds of small huts (median footprint 18.6-19.3 m2); 165,169 round houses in North + Far North; enclosures hardly mapped (87 closed in Far North)
West and North-West (Grassfields): dispersed family compounds around a yard; chefferies/fondoms (palace of the Fon or chief)
Centre, South, East: villages strung along roads in the forest; huge arrondissements with few buildings (Tcholliré 14,617 km2)
Coast and creeks: Wouri estuary and Bakassi landings; Lake Chad shore
settlement.census: RGPH-4 fieldwork 24 Apr - 15 Sep 2026, results not yet published; UN 2025 urban projections Yaoundé ~5.1 M, Douala ~4.1 M

walls.north: Far North 478 wall lines, 87 closed enclosures: saré enclosures (often seccos) mostly unmapped

numbers.rule: read in pairs, as Cameroonian phone numbers are: 2367 -> '23 67'; 5 digits -> '1 10 99'
numbers.ff: French numerals are commonly used for phone numbers in the North (to verify in the memorability study)

spelling.note: Spelling words for spot codes, Cameroonian places first; G/J and M/N are the pairs most often confused aloud

plateName.rule: The name in the remembered code is a short PLATE NAME, because a long official name is neither said nor written in full: at most 12 characters (letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes; an accented letter is one) and at most 2 words (linking words de, du, des, la, le, of, the do not count; a hyphen separates words: 'Mvog-Ada' is 2 words), no digits
plateName.officialName: the full name from the map is kept and printed in small type on cards and plates for context; never required
plateName.language: English generic words in the North-West and South-West, French elsewhere; both generic lists applied everywhere because names mix
derivation: 1. a documented short form people already say (none asserted for Cameroon yet)

2. clean: map spellings ('Ouro_kessoum_1' -> 'Ouro Kessoum I', a name all in capitals in title case, a number 1-10 as a Roman numeral as quartiers are written: 'Melen 8' -> 'Melen VIII'); drop brackets, text after a slash, generic words (Quartier, Lotissement, Zone, Village, Campement, Hameau, Chefferie (de), Community, Estate, Layout, Quarter, Town, Area) and a linking word they leave at an end
3. if it fits, that is the plate name ('Cité Des Palmiers' -> 'Palmiers' only because it does not fit; 'Cité SIC' stays)

4. else the best run of whole words, dropping head words first: Carrefour, Rond-point, Place, Rue, Montée, Entrée, Vallée, Pont, Station, Mission, Junction, Camp, Cité, and the Fulfulde settlement words of the North (Ouro/Wouro, Hosséré, Mayo, Djaouro/Djaoro, Ardo, Lawan)

5. Cameroon rule: an automatic short form may drop only head, generic and linking words; if it would drop another word of the name (a second proper name, a qualifier such as Upper, Ancien, II, PK 14), the commune chooses (needsCouncilChoice)

6. never a word cut, never a name equal to a commune seat, region capital or regional city other than the area's own (Douala, Yaoundé, Mokolo, Kribi, Dakar, Bangui...), never fewer than 4 letters automatically
plateName.hyphenated: local hyphenated names are names, not scheme labels: 'Mvog-Ada', 'Etoa-Meki', 'Biyem-Assi' are kept whole; one over 12 characters ('Mvog-Atangana-Mballa') goes to the commune
plateName.reduplication: a word written twice is a reduplicated name ('Louba Louba', 'Kouéssé-Kouéssé') and is kept
plateName.abbreviations: St, Ste, Mt are allowed and read as Saint, Sainte, Mount by the name key
plateName.council: an area with needsCouncilChoice has up to 3 plateCandidates and a provisional plate name (the first), under which its codes are issued; the commune may confirm or replace it once, and the provisional name stays an alias
plateName.aliases: the official name typed in full decodes when it maps to one plate name (names.json aliases); an alias claimed by two plate names, or equal to another plate name, is dropped and listed in aliasesDropped

fields.name: plate name used in the code
fields.plateRule: as-is | cleaned | abbreviated | known | distinctive | council

area.what: quartier / quarter / village / chefferie quarter / lamidat quarter people already name

area.uniqueness: national, by plate name: see nationalNames

homeCode.number: 3, 4 or 5 digits (never more: five is the most people say and remember as a pair and a hundred), from the plate name's national range; each area a frozen block of max(20, ceil(2c/10)*10) numbers (engine/SPEC.md 2.4)

check.over: national name id (6 digits) + block index (2 digits) + number
check.where: plates, forms, QR, machine form only
check.catches: every single wrong digit, every swap of neighbouring digits

homeCode.rememberedFormValidation: registry sparsity (about half the numbers issued) + gate photo, quartier and commune shown before navigation

options.chosen: when the name's combined national blocks exceed 9,000 numbers

homeCode.uniqueness: Name + number is unique in all Cameroon on its own; city/arrondissement on the plate is information only
homeCode.machineForm: CM-<zone key>-<area index 3>-<number>-<Damm check over nameId5 + zoneIndex3 + area + number>; the check is for systems, never shown to people

spotCode.form: CM-<zone> E<east> N<north>, e.g. CM-DLA1 E0449 N0268
spotCode.digits: 4 per axis, 5 where the zone frame is wider than 99.99 km
spotCode.origin: zone box south-west corner floored to 0.01 degree; reference latitude: box centre rounded to 0.01 degree
spotCode.alternativeConsidered: a 3 m grid with letters 23456789CFGHJMPQRVWX and a check character, set aside because people remember names and numbers, not grid letters

groupingRules.name: closed OSM wall/fence/hedge 40-20,000 m2, smallest ring
open-wall: snap open OSM wall segments (3 m) to each other, road edges and facades; polygonise; faces 40-20,000 m2 are enclosures (Douala 105,306 segments / 2,222 km; Yaoundé 63,887 / 1,918 km)
saré: closed wall or seccos ring with several huts (North, Far North, Adamaoua)
N-Ways gated compound (outer level: estates, camps, government, military, police, sites)
annex: < 40 m2 joins nearest >= 2x within 8 m (towns)
yard cluster: walls within 6 m around a shared yard, one structure >= 60 m2, split at 15 m (Grassfields, forest villages)

compound.estates: two levels: estate gate then compound gate (SIC camps, MAETUR estates, company camps)
compound.regrouping: never changes an issued code: merge -> alias; split -> old code on one part, new numbers from the gap
compound.numbering: Hilbert order (order 16 over the area box) of main gates (else compound centres), spread evenly over the number range

compound.use: one-household | multi-household | mixed | commercial | institutional | outbuildings-only
compound.name: business/public only

sub.maison: one-storey house in dur (default urban dwelling)
sub.immeuble: apartment block (Akwa, Bonanjo, Bastos, centre-ville); floors >= 4 or OSM apartments; units by '#'

sub.case: village house of earth/thatch or poto-poto; rural, small, OSM hut
sub.case-ronde: round house / saré hut; circularity > 0.88 and < 60 m2
sub.compound-house: house of a Grassfields family compound (yard-cluster rule)
sub.dependance: boys' quarters / annex rooms; inside compound, < 40 m2 or people

sub.boutique: shop, often in the compound's front wall (shopfront entrance)
sub.marche: market (Mokolo, Marché Central, Sandaga, Mboppi, Mvog-Mbi); OSM marketplace or N-Ways market

memorabilityEvaluation.design: randomised: half the pilot households get a place+4-digit code, half are shown the same home as an alphanumeric spot code; both with plate + app
measures: free recall after 1 day, 1 week, 1 month (exact / one-digit error / wrong)
time to say or type the code
first-time arrival success of couriers using the code
errors caught by the check digit or the gate photo
targets: exact recall after a week >= 80% for place+digits
digit-level errors caught or shown wrong gate >= 95%

stats.note: figures of the paper (docs/paper.md); counted on the issued registry

precedence.rule: Where the government, a council or Campost already gives an address, it is shown first, exactly as written; every compound also has its N-Ways code.

order.source: Council street + door number (CUD metric numbering since 1992; CUY numbered streets 'Rue 1794', 'No 1232'; other councils)
OSM addr:street + addr:housenumber copied from a plate (confirmed)

order.when: every compound; shown after ranks 1-3 where they exist

precedence.areaCodes: Campost commune postal codes stored in zones.json campostCode and shown beside any address; N-Ways codes nest inside them
precedence.later: When an official address appears for a door, it becomes primary; the N-Ways code becomes an alias (superseded_by) so old plates and links still work
precedence.poBox: A BP is a mailbox, never an address
precedence.ifCampostNational: If Campost-FindMe proves working and national, this repo becomes an integration plan: no new format; app imports and shows Campost addresses; Add my home points to the PLP
precedence.currentEvidence: Official door addresses cover a small part of Douala and Yaoundé and an unknown number of PLP holders; most of Cameroon has nothing official
precedence.coverage: per zone: share of compounds with a PLP, share of entrances with an official number, published in model/stats/official-coverage.json once official data is published

nationalNames.rule: A plate name and number must be unique nationally on their own: many neighbourhoods share a name, and a code read aloud carries no town
nationalNames.normalise: strip accents and case; remove spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, dots; Roman numerals and FR/EN number words to digits; St/Ste/Mt to Saint/Sainte/Mount (Nkol-Bisson = Nkolbisson; Mile Four = Mile 4; Ndogpassi III = Ndogpassi 3)

allocation.range: one national range per normalised plate name: 1000-9999 if all blocks fit, else 10000-99999
allocation.block: one frozen block per area, size max(500, ceil(2 x buildings / 100) x 100), laid out in zone order
allocation.spare: rest of the range free for new same-name areas (next free block) and overflow blocks of full areas
allocation.qualifier: only if a name's blocks exceed 90,000 numbers: split once by an established qualifier people say (town), recorded in names.json
allocation.frozen: blocks never move; numbers never change

nationalNames.decode: normalise name -> national entry (or alias of an official name -> its plate name) -> block holding the number -> area, zone, compound
